Preparing for an IT audit: the information that makes a difference.

A useful audit starts with a clear scope and accessible evidence.

← All insights

Clarify the starting question

Define the decisions the audit should inform: assessing access controls, reviewing continuity or examining governance. An explicit scope avoids collecting too much information and producing unfocused conclusions.

Gather useful documents

The IT organisation chart, application map, policies, procedures, inventories and continuity plans are a starting point. Supplement them with evidence of implementation: access reviews, tickets, meeting notes and test results.

Identify the right stakeholders

Involve the people responsible for the activities being reviewed and plan for their availability. Discussions should establish how things actually work, beyond written procedures.

Prepare for what follows the audit

Plan a presentation that distinguishes findings, risks and recommendations. Assign an owner and a realistic deadline to each agreed action.

This guidance is general. The appropriate scope and measures depend on the context of your organisation.
